implementerProof.how: Review 5706963620's three findings were each driven at this head. (1) The High, round 6's label check refusing a correctly pinned row: I confirmed the reviewer's premise myself with an anonymous Docker Hub read — `library/nats:2.15.1-alpine` resolves today to sha256:7ae34c25…, while the row pins sha256:2ae57dfb…, so that check would have refused an honest row, and this pull request retags every row, so every tagged row would have reached it. The read is gone: the only `crane digest` calls left in mirror-ci-images.sh name the package's own tag (:126 and :134), never an upstream tag. Its harness prints `32 passed, 0 failed`, 30 before. (2) The binding the deleted check was there for is now where an image or a build can carry it, and I drove both halves. Go: the pinned row's own bytes do declare their version — reading the manifest index, the linux/amd64 manifest and the config blob of docker.io/library/golang@sha256:8a5910f3… anonymously gives `GOLANG_VERSION=1.27.1`, the version the row's tag names. Driving mirror-ci-images.sh from a fixture with a stub crane: a held golang row whose config says 1.26.3 under a 1.27.1-alpine label fails before anything is held or copied, naming the source, both versions and what to write; one whose config declares no GOLANG_VERSION fails saying so; the matching one prints `go … carries Go 1.27.1, the version its upstream tag names` and both rows are held, exit 0 — and in that same run the nats row, whose upstream names its own digest, gets no label line at all, which is the case round 6's check got wrong. Bun: oven/bun declares no version, so the build decides, and the web stage's RUN is the decision. I ran its logic against a stub `bun`: 1.4.4 against a .bun-version of 1.4.4 passes, 1.4.5 exits 1 with the message naming both. That the stage can read .bun-version at all is a build input, and `check-image-trigger-paths.sh` passes with `every image trigger covers every input its build reads (5 image build(s))`, which is the gate that holds the listener image's triggers to it. (3) The two minors: `upstream_parts` writes out Docker Hub's implicit `library/`, which I drove on the real tree — both golang rows respelled `docker.io/golang:…` leave rule 3 satisfied (no false `no row copies library/golang`), and a FROM moved onto a short-spelled next-version row still fires rule 7 by name, which is the escape the thermonuclear passes found; and the copy's output sentence now matches what my fixture runs print. Every other harness and gate is green at this head: check-ci-images 99 (96 before), check-bun-version 119, select-e2e-proofs 94, ci-ok 40, the tree mode with 12 rows and 35 references, the filter gate with 25 gates, every remote action pinned, no private name over 6,323 files, and 58 job definitions with no non-call job lacking a timeout.
